newsitem.title: GERMANY: Jochimsen labels Buba's fight with Bonn dramatic.
newsitem.headline: Jochimsen labels Buba's fight with Bonn dramatic.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen said on Friday that the government's plans to revalue currency and gold reserves marked a "dramatic conflict" with the Bundesbank.
"We have a dramatic conflict which must be played out fully in public," he told Reuters in an interview.
But Jochimsen also said there was no question that members of the Bundesbank's policy-making council would resign over this conflict with Bonn, which he said was unprecedented.
"In the past we always tried to achieve an agreed solution in disputes. In this regard, the government's present actions are a complete break in style," he said.

Jochimsen, who reiterated that the Bundesbank found Bonn's revaluation plans unacceptable, said German Finance Minister Theo Waigel had gone ahead with the project despite obvious massive reservations from the Bundesbank, which were made clear 15 days ago.
"An agreeable solution has to be found quickly or there will be disastrous consequences," he said.
The full scale of the crisis was not yet clear, he added, with neither financial markets nor the public as yet fully aware of what Waigel's gold plans would actually mean.
"The central bank council has already made absolutely clear statements and it will continue to do so. The mood on the council is determined and resignations are out of the question," Jochimsen said.

The Bundesbank on Wednesday issued a statement rejecting the German government's plans to revalue central bank reserves, saying the concept clashed with Maasstricht rules and was an intervention into the Bundesbank's own monetary policy.
Finance Minister Theo Waigel has vowed to proceed with the plans, which envisage distributing part of the gain in value from these reserves to redeem old debts.
